summary: check_car looks up a prim named RollingRoadFrame that the environment never authors, so the belt frame width, the spare-clearance figure and the underbody footprint use the belt width instead.
failure_scenario: by_name(parts,'RollingRoadFrame') returns None, so fr_hw falls back to half the belt width (48.5) instead of the frame half width (60, from RollingRoadPlates). The report states the belt 'with its frame it is 97.0 wide' with '28.8 to spare each side' (true: 120 wide, 17.3 spare), and the 'inner_track > fr_hw' pass test and the underbody 'over' mask use 48.5. A car whose inner tyre face sat between 48.5 and 60 cm would pass 'Belt runs between the wheels' while touching the frame.
evidence: Static trace. build_env.py defines RollingRoadBelt, RollingRoadSlot, RollingRoadDrums and RollingRoadPlates only; test_section.usda lists those four Mesh defs and RollingRoadPlates extent is (-60,-321,-3)..(60,507,0.25). Committed models/wind_tunnel/docs/fit-check.md line 181 prints 'with its frame it is 97.0 wide' and '28.8 to spare'. Not executed (needs the blueprint clone and pxr).

summary: The jet-window clearance is measured only from mesh vertices to the domain rectangle, but the straight top wall has no vertices over the domain, so the reported clearance is too large and a low top wall would not be caught.
failure_scenario: u_profile places vertices only at the foot points and on the corner arcs, so the flat roof between x=-285 and x=285 has no vertex near |x|<=144. For the nozzle exit (hw 325, h 400, r 40) the vertex minimum is 181.0 (side wall) while the true roof-to-domain-top gap is 152.0; for the collector throat 256.0 vs 252.0. The guide and fit report publish 181.0 and 256.0 as the 'smallest' clearances and justify vertex sampling by corner chord error only. If exit_h were 240 (roof inside the domain, z<248) every vertex still has dx>0 (141) and n_in==0, so 'Domain sits inside the jet' would PASS while the wall crosses the domain; the Y-range AABB test cannot catch it because the nozzle is far upstream.
evidence: Standard-library probe replicating mesh_compute._profile and rect_dist: nozzle inner vertex-min 181.0 vs h-248=152; nozzle outer 206.0 vs 177; collector inner 256.0 vs 252. build_env.py check() prints the true 'top' row (152.0), so the two reports disagree. Probe run on CPU with python -I; the h=240 case is by arithmetic on the same vertex set, not a built scene.

summary: The NaN guard runs after saveStage, so a NaN-bearing file is left on disk even though the project states the build scripts refuse to save one.
failure_scenario: If an intermittent NaN matrix is authored, ux.saveStage writes test_section.usda, then the regex raises RuntimeError. The bad asset remains at its published path and later tools (build_present, render, fit_check) consume it. The same ordering is in build_present.py lines 389-392 for present.usda and present_payload.usda.
evidence: Source order: saveStage at build_env.py:776, read_text/regex at 777-778; build_present.py saveStage at 389, regex at 390. CLAUDE.md says 'The build scripts refuse to save a file that contains NaN'. Not executed.

summary: Override layer: payload is an explicit list-op, relative sublayer and payload paths resolve from models/wind_tunnel/scenes to external/blueprint and assets/test_section.usda, metadata matches the stage contract (Z-up, 0.01, 60 tcps); fit_check composition checks assert the same.

Mesh kits (meshlib, mesh_compute): profile ordering, loft indexing, disc/annulus/tube winding, sweep frames for U paths and diagonal members, and resample arithmetic traced by hand and found consistent; nozzle/collector probe-face outward orientation indexes the intended inner top-centre strip.

texture_compute: radix-2 FFT direction, spectrum filter, per-map seeds (no overlap), tile periodicity for perforation/honeycomb/belt, sRGB and OpenGL normal conventions are consistent; honeycomb normal scale uses tile x for both axes (about 1 percent off), judged cosmetic.

Orbit spline: CPU-only reimplementation of closed_spline with the ORBIT control points gives one monotone full turn, exact closure, max eye Y 654 (well clear of the 762.5 nozzle lip), and velocity/acceleration jumps at the wrap of 6.4e-05 / 1.1e-05, inside check_presentation tolerances.

Dolly/Orbit sample times (frame*60/fps), stage end time 900 in present.usda (360 steps * 2.5), interpolation clearance bound (half the longest segment) and check_stilts geometry were traced and are consistent; point_tri_dist matches Ericson region priority order.

build_share path guard, zip determinism and integrity verification, and build_media fixed allowlist read correctly; smoke.py time units (seconds = frame/24) and the pxr/ovrtx process split hold, since ovrtx is imported lazily in rtx.py; field_view hash re-check, destination guard and PLY layout validation are sound, and it runs GPU kernels without GpuPacer, which I did not count as a defect because it is a one-shot tool and not a worker.
